comparator.name: Computer Science
comparator.academicYear: Current programme and 2026-2027 course continuity checked 2026-10-07; latest complete official curriculum table 2025-2026
comparator.sourceNotes: The current programme and live 2026-2027 course records confirm the continuing Dutch-taught Computer Science bachelor and its programming, mathematical, systems, data and AI curriculum. The latest complete target-specific programme table supplies one coherent 180-EC pathway. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 EC of compulsory study. The third year contains 30 EC of genuine minor/free-choice space, 15 EC for the Bachelor Thesis Project, 3 EC of AI and Ethics, 6 EC of Software Engineering and 6 EC of advanced free-choice study, instantiated by the first-listed eligible 6-EC option Applied Data Science and Explainable AI. The guide displays Machine Learning in both Years 2 and 3 because it serves transitioning cohorts; the coherent entrant pathway counts it once in Year 2 and uses the separately documented 6-EC Year-3 choice instead. The target is the standard Computer Science bachelor, not the separately normalized Data Science and Artificial Intelligence programme or a double/combined route.
components: Genuine minor/free-choice space; no subject invented.
Required independent computer-science research and development project.
Advanced elective: Applied Data Science and Explainable AI
First-listed eligible 6-EC advanced choice from the official curriculum.

core: Programming, software engineering, databases, operating systems, networks and computer systems
Algorithms, data structures, formal reasoning and computational problem-solving
Mathematical foundations of computing: discrete mathematics, calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics
Data science, machine learning, data mining, visualisation and prediction
Artificial-intelligence reasoning, optimisation, learning and intelligent-system design
Computer-science research methods, team software work, scientific problem-solving and an independent bachelor thesis
adjacent: Human cognition and computational models of information processing
Human-computer interaction, cybersecurity and responsible computing
Data visualisation and scientific discovery from large or complex datasets
Language, media and interaction in computational systems
questions: How do algorithms, software and systems turn real problems into reliable computation?
How can data-driven and intelligent systems be designed, evaluated and used responsibly?

trace: teaches research design, operationalization, experimental design and sampling together with descriptive and inferential statistics; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the study of experiments, observational data, bias and summary statistics that Leiden's Principles of Data Science treats

examines AI fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility, the moral status of AI systems and the philosophical and psychological questions about human-AI interaction; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the philosophical issues raised by AI that Leiden University treats in Philosophy & Artificial Intelligence

teaches planning for AI systems in deterministic and non-deterministic environments with uncertainty, partial observability and optimisation under constraints; it directly implements the planning and decision-making under uncertainty strand of the core, treated by Leiden University in Reasoning Techniques and Operations Research

covers logic, discrete mathematics, patterns and structures with applications to computer science and algorithm construction; it directly implements the discrete-mathematics and logic foundation of the core

covers uninformed and informed search, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction and convex, linear and non-linear optimisation by rational agents with laboratory work; it directly implements the search and optimisation methods of Leiden's Reasoning Techniques

teaches reinforcement-learning frameworks and algorithms and has students build agents with neural networks that learn by trial and error; it directly implements the behaviour-learning agents of Leiden's Intelligent Systems

covers Internet architecture and protocols together with operating-system processes, scheduling, concurrency, memory and file systems; it directly implements the networks and operating-systems strand of Leiden's compulsory core
introduces relational database theory, SQL, normalization and query processing; it directly implements the database content of the core

teaches software planning, requirements gathering, testing, quality assurance, maintenance and code review through projects in C++ and Haskell; it directly implements the software-engineering strand of the core
teaches algorithm design and analysis, data structures and experimental performance analysis with laboratory work; it directly implements the algorithms and data-structures strand of the core

studies modern algebraic algorithms and solution methods for optimisation problems with algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the algorithmic problem-solving and optimisation content that Leiden's core addresses in graph theory, algorithms and linear programming

teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation, including spatial and text data, and ends with an own research project analysing data; it directly implements the data-science process of exploring and preparing data that Leiden's introductory data-science course and Data Analysis address

teaches linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering on real data; it directly implements the machine-learning strand of the core

teaches camera and image models, feature detection and the processing, analysis and understanding of image data with programming; it makes a specific complementary contribution as a data-science application of machine learning to visual data, the territory of Leiden's image and video processing elective

builds neural networks from scratch and in TensorFlow, applies them to vision and text and studies large language models; it directly implements the deep-learning side of machine learning and the neural-language-model content that Leiden University addresses in Natural Language Processing

treats kinematics, motion and manipulation of autonomous robots and the computational problems they raise; it makes a specific complementary contribution to intelligent agents acting in physical environments, which Leiden's Intelligent Systems treats with robots as an agent type

teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python with testing and debugging, and elements of discrete mathematics and computational problem solving; it directly implements the programming foundation of the core, which Leiden University teaches in Procedural Programming and Objects in Programming
teaches differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations through projects; it directly implements the calculus foundation of the mathematical core
teaches matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations; it directly implements the linear-algebra foundation of the mathematical core and of machine learning

teaches numerical methods for root finding, differentiation and differential equations with attention to algorithm accuracy; it directly implements the numerical-methods strand of the mathematical core

extends calculus to several dimensions and differential equations with computer algebra software for data analysis; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the multivariable calculus underlying optimisation and neural-network training

characterises linear time-invariant systems through impulse and frequency response, convolution, Fourier representations and transfer functions; it directly implements the dynamical-systems side of mathematical modelling taught in Leiden's Mathematical Modelling
covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; it directly implements the probability-and-statistics foundation of the core

introduces central themes of Western philosophy on knowledge, consciousness and responsibility, their relation to computer science and psychology and the methods of philosophical argument; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the philosophical foundation for the philosophy-of-science and philosophy-of-AI content of the programme

examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism and practical ethics; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the ethical theory needed to analyse the moral questions raised by intelligent systems

asks whether the mind can be explained neurobiologically and whether artificial systems, including large language models, can be conscious; it directly implements the philosophical issues about replicating human consciousness and intelligence that Leiden University treats in Philosophy & Artificial Intelligence

explores the neural mechanisms of perception and action and how the brain guides goal-directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience; it directly implements the perception and action topics of the cognitive-neuroscience strand

deepens neurophysiology and experimental cognitive neuroscience and treats memory, attention, executive function, emotion, social cognition and decision making; it directly implements the learning, memory and decision topics of cognitive neuroscience, which Leiden University includes among the cognitive models relevant to knowledge engineering

examines how people acquire, produce and understand language, with the neuroscience of language, experimental approaches and links to computer science; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the human counterpart of the computational language processing in Leiden's Natural Language Processing

introduces functional brain anatomy, neuronal communication and the psychological and neuroscientific study of perception, learning and behaviour; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the cognitive and biological psychology that Leiden University teaches in Computational and Cognitive Neuroscience, without covering its modelling of cognition

teaches multivariate statistical models, regression, logistic regression, factor analysis and experimental methods; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the applied data analysis (multiple regression, classification and dimensionality reduction) of Leiden's Data Analysis

develops precise persuasive writing and presentation through rhetorical analysis and practice; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the communication of technical arguments and research that Leiden develops through Studying and Presenting

alternatives.label: Computer science, software & systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines UCR's full available computer-science sequence with mathematical foundations, data and AI, research methods, communication and philosophy. The label foregrounds the programming, algorithms, software, database, network and operating-system core without implying UCR offers Leiden's complete hardware and theoretical sequence.
alternatives.concept: A computer-science-centred programme built around programming, algorithms and data structures, databases, networks and operating systems, software development, advanced algorithms and mathematical foundations, supported by data science, machine learning, AI, research methods, communication and responsible-computing inquiry.
progression: Introduction to Programming and Logic & Discrete Mathematics establish programming and formal foundations in semester 1. Mathematical Methods in semester 2 precedes all dependent mathematics; Introduction to Programming precedes Networks & Operating Systems, Algorithms & Data Structures, Software Development, Advanced Algorithms and later AI courses. Networks & Operating Systems is taken at its sole planned offering in semester 3. Research Methods and foundational mathematics precede advanced computational, data and AI work. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed earlier.

alternatives.label: Computer science, data & machine learning
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum retains programming, databases, algorithms, software and mathematics while shifting four courses from the closest route toward computer vision, robotics, experimental statistics and brain-and-behaviour foundations. Its centre is computational work with data and learning systems rather than software and systems alone.
alternatives.concept: A computational data-science route linking programming, databases, algorithms, software and mathematical modelling with probability, experimental statistics, machine learning, neural networks, computer vision, robotics, optimisation and decision-making under uncertainty.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this programme replaces Networks & Operating Systems, Advanced Algorithms, rhetorical communication and general philosophy with Computer Vision, Robotics, Statistics & Experimental Methods and Introduction to Brain & Behavior. The different courses are direct consequences of its data, learning and embodied-intelligence focus, not numerical substitutions.
progression: Introduction to Programming, Introduction to Data Science and Logic & Discrete Mathematics establish computational foundations in semester 1. Mathematical Methods and Database Management Systems in semester 2 precede dependent mathematics and advanced work. Algorithms, linear algebra, probability and computer vision in semester 3 precede software, numerical methods, robotics, machine learning, neural networks, optimisation and reinforcement learning. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed earlier.

alternatives.label: Artificial intelligence, cognition & responsible systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines computing, mathematics, machine learning and AI with perception, higher cognition, language, philosophy of mind and ethics. The label accurately describes its different educational choice: intelligent systems examined together with human cognition, interaction and responsibility.
alternatives.concept: An artificial-intelligence route connecting programming, machine learning, neural networks, optimisation, robotics, vision and decision-making with perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, experimental methods, ethics and philosophy of mind.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the other routes, this programme replaces much of the dedicated software, systems and advanced mathematics sequence with cognitive science, psychology and philosophy. Its organising question is how intelligent systems learn, perceive, interact and raise questions of responsibility, rather than how to build a broad software/systems or data-science curriculum.
progression: Introduction to Programming, Introduction to Data Science and Introduction to Brain & Behavior open semester 1. Mathematical Methods, AI Ethics and Perception & Action follow in semester 2. Logic, linear algebra, probability and machine learning precede advanced neural networks, optimisation, robotics, decision-making, reinforcement learning and computer vision. Higher Order Functions and Psycholinguistics follow the brain-and-behaviour gateway and Perception & Action; Introduction to Western Philosophy precedes Philosophy of Mind. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed earlier.

candidates.label: Artificial intelligence, cognition and responsible interaction

selection.assessment: The closest alternative owns Computer Science's programming, algorithms, software, databases, networks, operating systems and mathematical foundations. The target evidence also supports two coherent and materially different directions: data and statistical learning, and artificial intelligence linked to cognition, interaction and responsible systems. Their schedules replace substantial groups of systems/software or data-oriented courses with concept-driven alternatives, and every pair differs by at least four courses. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both establish structured and object-oriented programming, testing, debugging and computational problem-solving foundations.
Both cover operating-system resource management and Internet architecture and protocols through practical computational work.
Both cover relational databases, SQL, data modelling, normalization and query processing.
Both develop software through requirements, design, implementation, testing, maintenance and quality assurance.
Both teach algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis.
Advanced Algorithms addresses computational efficiency and algorithmic solution methods, while Leiden's component gives a dedicated formal treatment of complexity.
Both develop the structured communication and presentation of academic or technical arguments; Leiden situates this specifically in computer-science study.
UCR has one introductory programming course and a later software-development course, but no separate second compulsory programming-techniques module at Leiden's weight.
UCR does not offer a dedicated digital logic and hardware-design course.
UCR's Networks & Operating Systems discusses hardware/software interaction but does not reproduce a dedicated computer-architecture course.
UCR Software Development uses C++ and Haskell but does not reproduce Leiden's separate programming-language-concepts component.
UCR includes responsible-computing and systems perspectives but no dedicated technical cybersecurity course in the fixed portfolio.
Both establish calculus and mathematical problem-solving used in computing.
Both cover matrices, vector spaces, transformations and eigenvalues.
Advanced Calculus extends the calculus foundation to multiple dimensions and differential equations.
Both establish probability distributions, inference and probabilistic reasoning for computing.
Both provide logic and discrete structures for formal computational reasoning.
No single UCR course reproduces Leiden's dedicated theoretical Foundations of Computer Science module.
UCR has no dedicated automata-theory component.
Algorithms & Data Structures is already aligned to Leiden's algorithms module and cannot be counted twice as the separate second-year data-structures course.
UCR has no dedicated formal-languages and computability course.
UCR offers one logic-and-discrete-mathematics course rather than Leiden's two-stage logic sequence.
Data science, machine learning & artificial intelligence
Both involve practical data preparation, analysis, visualization and interpretation, though Leiden's advanced elective adds explainable AI.
Both teach regression, classification, clustering and evaluation of predictive models.
Both examine fairness, responsibility, privacy and ethical questions raised by artificial intelligence.
Both cover computational search, optimisation and reasoning for artificial intelligence.
Both teach statistical modelling and experimental analysis, though Leiden frames the methods specifically for computer scientists.
Both develop research design, operationalisation, experiments, sampling and statistical inference; Leiden applies them specifically within computer science.
Both support academic orientation, study development and reflective professional formation.
UCR has no scheduled bachelor-thesis course; the standardized optional independent-research opportunity is placed against this component.
Leiden's genuine 30-EC minor or free-choice space is preserved without inventing a subject.

notes.text: Both curricula can include substantial programming, algorithms, databases, software development, operating systems, networks, mathematics, data science and artificial intelligence. Leiden additionally provides a fixed sequence in digital systems, computer architecture, automata, formal languages and computability, two-stage logic, technical security, programming-language concepts and a compulsory 15-EC thesis. UCR does not reproduce those specialist components at the same depth.

Leiden organises Computer Science as a tightly sequenced disciplinary bachelor with small-credit modules and a large third-year choice space. UCR distributes related study across 7.5-EC courses in computer science, mathematics, data science, artificial intelligence, cognition and philosophy, producing coherent liberal-arts routes rather than the same course-by-course structure.
